label: Pure perfection: Pure d: the determination d is an actuality that involves no potency, limitation…
definition: Pure d: the determination d is an actuality that involves no potency, limitation or reception. Determinations that are not pure are limiting, receiving or individuating principles, potencies or privations. The predicate is a parameter Pure : D → Prop.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#320), attribution deferred; compare the perfectiones simpliciter of the scholastic tradition (navigation only). Lean has no declaration for it: which determinations are pure is supplied by each interpretation. It is not the existing InAct relation, which says that a being is in act in a respect; everyPerfectionIsAllPureCase relates the two.
